name: mod-transcript
description: Restyles the transcript: your prompts and Claude's replies as chat bubbles, each finished turn folded under its prompt to one summary line (tools, file changes, skills, agents) with the final reply kept, each finished tool row folded to one line, Bash commands in shell colors, and a copy button under each reply. A click unfolds a turn or a call in place

fold_turns.title: Fold finished turns
fold_turns.description: Turns start folded to one line. The line sits under its prompt. Off, they start open and the line folds them

fold_tools.title: Fold tool rows
fold_tools.description: Each tool row folds to one line. Finished rows have their own toggle. Off, tool rows draw as Claude Code draws them

timestamps.title: Show times
timestamps.description: Prompt send time, tool duration. Each prompt shows when you sent it, and each tool line when it started and how long it took. Off, rows show no times

expand_live.title: Show the latest turn in full
expand_live.description: Stays open until your next prompt. The latest turn shows every tool row and result as Claude Code draws them. Off, finished tool calls fold right away

copy_pill.title: Copy button
copy_pill.description: On each finished reply's edge. A copy button sits there: point at it to pick reply, code, text, table or links, then click one. The reply marks what the choice under the pointer copies. Off, the edge stays plain

prompt_numbers.title: Prompt numbers
prompt_numbers.description: #N before each of your prompts. It matches the number the Prompts and Heads up panels show

animations.title: Animations
animations.description: The fold chip and the kind chips fade when the pointer leaves them, a running command's dot blinks, and the tabs and settings fade. Off, they switch at once and the dot stays lit

icons.title: Icons
icons.description: auto picks Nerd Font or safe glyphs. It uses Nerd Font icons when the terminal's font is a Nerd Font, read from Windows Terminal, iTerm2, VS Code, Ghostty, kitty, WezTerm, Alacritty, GNOME Terminal or Konsole, and safe Unicode glyphs elsewhere. nerd and safe force one
